description: Raggedness penalty curve. The three-way gate rejected batch padding by 105-209%, so cost is essentially PACKED -- but the most ragged cell ran 19.5% over the packed prediction while a moderate one ran 0.9% over. This sweeps the spread at fixed n and fixed total tokens to measure how that penalty grows, which is now the real question: not whether raggedness costs 3.7x, but whether it costs anything worth scheduling around.
note_controls: The two max_len=512 cells are uniform, so all three models predict the same cost. They cannot distinguish anything and are not meant to: they check the MEASUREMENT. If a control disagrees with every model, the verdict on the ragged cells is untrustworthy.
note_budget: Batch-padded totals are allowed to exceed max_num_batched_tokens here, unlike the gate run: that constraint existed only to keep the batch-padding PREDICTION in-budget for a clean three-way test, and batch padding is now rejected. Under packed behaviour the step holds total_tokens regardless of spread, so nothing splits.
note_separation: Predicted costs at n=4, total=2048, max=1536 are 39.2 / 56.6 / 144.8 ms for packed / per-request-padded / batch-padded -- a 3.7x spread, far outside the measurement noise, so the cell decides rather than hints.
note_spread: max_len is the only variable; n and total tokens are held exactly. The uniform cells (max_len=512) remain controls.
